title: Explain that more simply
source: Percent Session, the Learner's ask for the simple version (TUTOR_SPEC section 7, T4)

history.learner: ok I'm ready, teach me this
history.tutor:
Say a savings rate goes from 4% to 5%. The move is 5% minus 4%, which is 1 percentage point. A basis point is one hundredth of a percentage point, so that same move is 100 basis points. Compared with where it started, a rise of 1 point on 4% is a rise of 25 percent of the old rate. Traders quote moves in basis points, and headlines often use percent, so always say which one you mean.
Which of the three would you use to tell a friend how far the rate moved?
